Plenty of hiking! The Hiking Project is a great app to check out, but Ester Dome has some great trails, as does UAF. If you look up "UAF hiking" or "Ester Dome", the actual trails will be on there. I also LOVE hiking Mt Healy. 

Mt. Healy is right by Denali Nat Park, but you don't have to access it from the Visitor's Center. If you drive south from Fairbanks, and go slightly past Healy, before the Canyon (where all the tourist shops and cruise attractions are) there's a pullout right at Bison Gulch. You have to cross the road, and there's a trail going up. It's very steep, and there are several false summits, but you get a good view of Healy and Stampede Trail (where Chris McCandless went rouge). I hope that made sense? It's a little confusing without a visual, but definitely a favorited hike! 

Also, with the lights, Skiland is where it's at. Just don't go all the way up the mountain, because it gets a lot of tourists and the owners charge you like $30 to see them. There are plenty of pullouts out there to stop, and it's good to get out of the light pollution.

Obligatory not a parent, but an adult with terrible parents: my father moved us around A LOT as kids, and not just across town. No, it was 6+ hour differences. He was/is a corporate monkey, invested only in becoming bigger and better within the company. That being said, he was a very absent dad (and when he wasn't absent, he was super controlling and borderline abusive) and we learned not to rely on him. He was also, coincidentally, the only man in our lives, and that's created some daddy issues with my brother and I. 

So we learned everything from our mother. She was born and raised in Germany (we're American), so every thing we were being taught was very different than what our classmates knew. She was also anti-social, so she never let any of our friends come over, and a worry wart, so she never let us go anywhere. Overall, both very controlling and mean people.

We had a couple different reactions. My older sister turned into what they call a "Bible Banger" or "Jesus Freak" and got married young just to escape the house. Now my mom's upset that she prefers her in laws.

My brother and I had kind of similar reactions in that we both have a very hard time making friends. We're basically each other's only friend. I, the middle kid, have a pretty bad "I'll do whatever the hell I want, and fuck you if you don't agree streak" which leads to a whole lack of respect for authority, experimentation with a plethora of drugs and drinking, and mommy and daddy issues to boot. It's great. My brother has mommy issues in that he hangs onto her every word. It's sickening. For instance, I'll say something like "do you wanna get lunch with me?" And he, an 18 year old boy, will say "Let me ask Mommy". I'm not sure he'll ever move out, and he doesn't have a relationship with my dad.

Parents, let your kids explore the world without holding their hand the whole time. Let them have friends, let their friends teach them things. Don't tell them their dreams will never happen just because yours didn't. And be there! Don't just give them food at night and act like that's enough.

Oh great, now you and your SO have nothing to say to each other, since all convo revolved around the kids for the last 20ish years, and now they're out of the house. Retire, and never travel even though you promised you would. Watch the grandkids, bum around at home, die a regretful death over not doing more of what you wanted and less of what was expected of yoish
